title: Adaptive prefetch topology for long-window Llama / Mistral / Qwen variants
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: For long-window workloads on Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants we see two correlated issues: (1) 95th/99th tail latency spikes caused by large KV-resident working sets during high-concurrency continuous batching, and (2) uneven GPU memory pressure due to static prefetching that doesn't account for per-variant layer access patterns. Goal: design and implement an adaptive prefetch topology and residency scoring mechanism that reduces peak GPU memory footprint, limits KV-related latency tail, and preserves generation quality for long-context requests.

Scope: prototype and validate a topology-aware prefetch + eviction policy, integrate into the runtime's KV manager, run experiments across representative variants (llama-70b, mistral-8x, qwen-14b-long) and long-window configs (8k, 32k, 65k). Deliver runtime feature flag, canary rollout path, and telemetry dashboards for residency and tail latency.

Why different: instead of only tuning prefetch window size globally, this task builds a layer-topology map per model variant (early, mid, late attention blocks) and uses an adaptive moving-average residency score per KV segment to drive prefetch depth and on-device placement. It also introduces a transient compressed-KV fallback for extreme pressure rather than immediate eviction, preserving quality under bursty traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive prefetch topology implemented in KV manager behind feature flag
End-to-end integration with continuous batching pipeline and routing so canary traffic can be routed to flag-enabled nodes
Experiments show >=10% reduction in peak GPU memory for 32k/65k windows on targeted variants without increasing median latency beyond 3ms
95th latency improvement of at least 8ms on average across tested variants or a documented trade-off and mitigation plan
Automated regression tests for correctness of KV residency accounting and prefetch control
Dashboard widgets added to Console: per-variant residency heatmap, prefetch depth histogram, and fallback activation counts
Rollout plan documented with canary criteria and rollback steps
technical_notes: Topology map: during model load we compute logical buckets (early/mid/late) based on block index percentiles and persist map in variant metadata
Residency score: exponential moving average of accesses per KV segment (per-token touch) scaled by sequence position; score drives target prefetch depth per bucket
Prefetch policy: target_depth(bucket) = base_depth * f(residency_score, batch_size, seq_len_distribution)
Eviction strategy: soft-evict -> compress -> hard-evict. Compress uses 4-bit KV quant path if supported by model variant kernels; compression is transient for hot-to-warm transitions
Memory placement: prefer pinned slab for early buckets (high reuse) and pageable pinned regions for late buckets to allow GMM to reclaim under pressure
Batch-shaping: integrate with continuous-batcher to bias batch composition heuristics to keep working set locality (group requests with similar recent-seq prefixes)
Fallback: when compressed-KV activation rate exceeds threshold we trigger traffic shedding policies (gradual degrade to smaller model variant or increased batching) as last resort
Metrics: per-variant kv_residency_score, prefetch_depth_actual, prefetch_depth_target, compress_activation_count, soft_evict_count, hard_evict_count
test_plan: Unit tests for topology map generation and residency score updates
Local integration tests with synthetic long-context traces simulating prefix-heavy and suffix-heavy access patterns
Perf runs on dedicated test cluster with 8x llms across 8k/32k/65k windows; record P50/P95/P99 latency, GPU mem peak, tokens/sec
A/B canary: route 5% production traffic for 72h with detailed downstream correctness checks and compare model output differences on a curated prompt set
Chaos test: inject background memory pressure (other tenants synthetic allocation) and verify compress->evict transitions follow documented thresholds
